title: Fragile Packing for Electronics on Addis Cobblestone Routes
excerpt: Protect TVs, monitors, and glass on rough streets: double box, corner protectors, upright transport, and climate considerations.
content:
Why Addis streets matter

Cobblestone, speed bumps, and tight compound turns shock poorly packed screens. Original OEM boxes are best; otherwise use double-walled cartons and marked FRAGILE faces visible from the truck door.

Loading orientation

  • Keep TVs and monitors upright; never lay unboxed panels flat under weight.
  • Secure PCs with internal padding; remove loose hard drives if advised by IT.
  • Wrap glass table tops vertically with edge guards.
  • Fill void space in cartons so items cannot slide on turns.

Climate and dust

Electronics left on loading docks attract dust—seal boxes with tape and load electronics after soft goods when possible. Avoid storing heat-sensitive gear in closed trucks mid-day without ventilation.

Professional materials

Our packaging crew uses dish packs, bubble, and corner protectors—details on materials guide. Owner-packed fragile boxes should be noted on inventory before sign-off.

Claims and documentation

Photograph serial numbers at load; note existing scratches on monitors. Written scope should state whether electronics are included in declared move value.

Condo lifts

Pad lift walls when moving large TV cartons—management fines for scratches are separate from mover damage claims. See condo checklist.

TV size and lift doors

Measure lift interior before booking large panels. If the freight lift is too shallow, plan stair carry with enough crew—never force a diagonal tilt that cracks the bezel.
